description: The TuriX-CUA Multimodal Vision Pipeline adds visual AI capabilities to qontinui's agentic verification loop. When users run workflows with agentic verification architecture, the system can capture screenshots, annotate them with numbered element markers, and send annotated images to vision-capable LLMs (Claude API, Gemini API) for screen analysis. A two-phase Brain/Actor pattern splits expensive vision reasoning from cheap action execution. This spec covers the pages where these capabilities are configured (Settings > AI, Run Options Dialog), where results are displayed (Run Summary, Active Dashboard, AI Output), and where supporting features surface (Skills page for playbooks, action executor for click highlights). Data flows from the Rust backend through Tauri IPC commands to the React frontend.

groups.description: After an agentic verification workflow completes, the Run Summary page displays per-iteration results. Each iteration shows the verification verdict (Pass/Fail/Partial with confidence percentage), worker summary, and timing. When Brain/Actor mode was active, iterations additionally show the Brain's screen analysis and action plan injected into the worker context. Data is fetched via Tauri IPC commands (get_task_run, get_task_run_events) reading from the PostgreSQL task_runs and task_run_events tables.

groups.description: The agentic verification loop runs iterations of verification-agent followed by worker-agent until the goal is achieved or max_iterations is reached. Key automatic behaviors include: progressive iteration history compression (keeps context under 4000 chars), consecutive pass tracking (requires N passes before declaring success), and stop-signal responsiveness. When Brain/Actor mode is enabled, the Brain is invoked with multimodal prompts when should_invoke_brain() returns true (first iteration, cache expired, or RequestContext signal). The loop is orchestrated by LoopController in unified_workflow_executor/agentic_verification_loop.rs.
groups.name: Agentic Verification Loop Behavior

groups.description: The vision pipeline serves two user needs: (1) for developers automating their own web apps (UI Bridge white-box), it provides rich element data for intelligent verification without fragile selectors; (2) for automating third-party desktop apps (visual GUI black-box), it provides screenshot-based element detection with LLM vision reasoning. Users should understand which mode is active and why the system chose it.
groups.name: Vision Pipeline Purpose and Mental Model

groups.description: During automation execution, brief visual highlights appear at action locations (click, type, scroll targets). For UI Bridge apps, this is a CSS overlay injected by showClickHighlight() in debug/click-highlight.ts, called from action-executor.ts after each performAction() succeeds. Highlights use position:fixed, pointer-events:none, z-index:999999 to avoid interfering with the page. The animation is a pulsing circle that scales from 0.5 to 1.2 and fades from opacity 1 to 0 over 600ms.
groups.name: Click Highlight Visual Design
